paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this one. Hezekiah had just been given fifteen more years (Isaiah 38:5), and then company came knocking. He was so glad to see them that he showed them everything, and later he told Isaiah, "There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them" (Isaiah 39:4). I think a man who had just been rescued was still looking at his treasures when he should have been looking at the One who saved him.

Then comes the part that gets me. Isaiah tells him that everything in the palace, and some of his own descendants, will be carried off to Babylon (Isaiah 39:6-7). Hezekiah says the word of the LORD is good, and the text says he thought, "At least there will be peace and security in my lifetime" (Isaiah 39:8). I think that's the lesson, baker: it's easy to feel fine about a hard word when it lands on somebody else's calendar.

So ask yourself, friend: what am I showing off, and who is it all for? And when God's word is hard, am I only looking at my own days, or am I caring about the people who come after me? I burned a lot of batches before I learned to bake for the whole table and not just for myself. That's a good thing to check before the next batch goes in the oven.
